summary: Enterprise customer reports private deployment egress fee consuming trial buffer and unexpected prorated reserved-hours charge
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a one-off egress charge from their Private deployment was billed against their trial buffer credit, and at the same time a prorated negative line for reserved GPU hours appeared after an autoscale adjustment. Impact: Kestrel is seeing an unexpected reduction of trial credit and an extra charge impacting month-end forecast. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2; account tied to enterprise org 'Kestrel Health Inc.' Timeline: 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC - Private deployment autoscale event triggered scale-down. 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC - Customer observes invoice preview showing -$1,200 prorated reserved-hours line. 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC - Dashboard shows a $350 egress line attributed to private connector egress. 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC - Customer opened support chat and escalated to enterprise CS.

Requested outcome: Clarify why trial buffer credits were consumed by private-deploy egress and confirm whether the prorated reserved-hours charge is valid. If incorrect, request provisional credit and remediation plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs scheduled model warmup in private VPC causing brief egress transfer to backup region
2) Autoscaler makes scale-down event for dedicated pool (reserved-hours reconciliation window overlaps scale event),
3) Billing postback service processes postbacks out-of-order due to transient queue backpressure,
4) Console invoice preview shows trial buffer credit being applied to egress line and reserved-hours prorate applied to account
logs: Billing postback IDs: pbk_20260309_wnz12, pbk_20260309_wnz13. Private connector logs show egress event at 2026-03-09T22:12:37Z. Autoscaler event: autoscaler-event-87321 triggered scaleDown at 2026-03-09T22:10:03Z. Console trace-id for invoice preview: trace-inv-99512. No 5xx in postback service during window but increased queue length ~6000 msgs. Extracts attached in support case (CSV).
investigation_notes: 03/10 Aisha: Initial triage - appears to be a race between postback ordering and reserve-hour reconciliation job; trial buffer should not be consumed by private-egress lines per policy, reserve prorates should be computed after postback de-dupe.

03/10 Miguel: Checked postback ordering metrics - spike in consumer lag at 22:11-22:20 UTC. Two postbacks for same session got reordered; one was egress line, then reserved-hours adjustment applied after - ordering might have assigned buffer to egress before reserve credit reconciliation.

03/11 SRE (Jordan Li): Queue backpressure traced to a flaky downstream S3 write in billing-aggregator. Consumer retried and processed duplicate postbacks; dedupe key TTL misaligned with retry window. Opened infra PR to increase dedupe window (PR linked).

03/11 Billing (Renee): Policy audit confirms trial buffer should be applied to hosted-hosted usage only; private egress is eligible but should consume balance from enterprise billing pool, not trial buffer. Possible tag mismatch caused trial buffer to be selected as eligible balance.

03/11 Hypothesis: tag normalization change in a recent deploy may have removed the 'private_deploy' tag on postbacks, causing them to fall back to default billing allocation logic and consume trial credit. Combined with out-of-order reserved-hour reconciliation this explains both symptoms.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:01 - Kestrel Billing Lead (Olivia Chen): We saw the invoice preview and our finance team flagged the two lines; please advise ASAP, month-end closes on 3/15.
2026-03-10 10:24 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thank you Olivia — we've started an investigation and will share logs and a temporary mitigation. Assigned to Eng/SRE to check postback ordering.

2026-03-11 14:02 - Miguel Santos (SRE/Eng): Found a spike in billing-aggregator consumer lag due to S3 error; opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1284 to extend dedupe TTL and added extra logging. Working on provisional credit while we validate the fix.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Renee Park (Billing): Confirmed tag mismatch in postback normalization for certain private connectors retroactively for ~18 minutes. We recommend issuing a provisional credit while we replay corrected postbacks.

2026-03-12 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Provisional credit of $350 for the egress line applied to Kestrel's account pending replay; reserved-hours prorate flagged for reversal pending reconciliation job run 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC. Customer notified.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Olivia Chen (Kestrel): Thanks — please confirm when final invoice will reflect reversal.
action_items: 1) Engineering to deploy dedupe TTL fix and normalization patch to billing-postback (PR linked).
2) Billing to apply provisional credit for the egress line ($350) and prepare reversal for the incorrectly applied prorated reserved-hours (-$1,200) pending replay results.
3) SRE to run controlled replay of corrected postbacks for 2026-03-09 22:00-22:30 UTC window and validate invoice preview results in staging before production reversal.
4) Product Ops to add a monitoring alert for consumer lag > 300s for billing-aggregator and include dedupe TTL drift dashboard panels.
5) Follow-up postmortem and customer-facing summary due 2026-03-18.
resolution: Provisional credit applied for $350 egress line on 2026-03-12. PR 1284 merged to extend dedupe TTL and fix tag normalization. Controlled replay scheduled and run confirmed that the reserved-hours prorate was incorrectly applied; final reversal submitted and will appear on next invoice cycle. Postmortem and monitoring improvements planned; customer agreed to closure once final reversal is visible.
